examples.subject: Applied Chemistry for Engineers
examples.markdown:
i) The cell potential of Nickel metal hydride battery is invariant whereas that of lead acid battery drops with usage. (1 M)
Reason – the concentration of electrolyte is invariant as there is production of same amount of OH$^-$ ions as it is consumed in the electrode reactions. Therefore potential is constant. In lead acid battery at both anode and cathode there is consumption of electrolyte which tend to decrease its concentration inturn decreasing the potential

ii) Maintenance free lead acid batteries do not need top up (1 M)
Reason – In this the presence of catalyst converts the H$_2$ and O$_2$ produced during overcharging back into water or Replacement of Pb by Pb-Ca alloy prevents the electrolysis of water. Therefore there is no loss of water during overcharging. Therefore it doesn’t need top up

examples.subject: Applied Chemistry for Engineers
examples.markdown:
Calculate E.M.F. of the zinc - silver cell at 25 $^\circ$C when [Zn$^{2+}$] = 1.0 M and [Ag$^+$] = 10 M

Write the cell representation and cell reaction.

[Given: $E^\circ$Zn$^{2+}$/Zn = - 0.76 V and $E^\circ$Ag$^+$/Ag is 0.80 V at 25$^\circ$C].

Cell representation

Zn$|$Zn2+(1M)$||$Ag+(10M)$|Ag

Cell reaction:

Zn + 2Ag$^+$ $\rightarrow$ Zn2+ + 2Ag

$E^\circ_{cell}$ = $E^\circ_{cathode}$ - $E^\circ_{anode}$

= 0.80 - ( -0.76) = 1.56 V

$E_{cell}$ = $E^\circ_{cell}$ - (0.0591/2) log [1]/[10]2

= 1.56 - (0.0591/2) log [1]/[10]2

= 1.6191 V

examples.subject: Fundamentals of Electronics
examples.markdown:
Given:

$$
I_0 = 1\,pA \text{ at } 20^\circ C
$$

Find:

$$
I_D = ? \quad \text{at } 150^\circ C,\ V_D = 0.5V
$$

$$
r_d = ? \quad \text{at } 150^\circ C
$$

$$
I_0' = I_0\,2^{\frac{150-20}{10}}
$$

$$
I_0' = 1p\cdot 2^{13}
$$

$$
I_0' = 8.192\,nA
$$

$$
V_T = \frac{T}{11600} = \frac{150+273}{11600} = \frac{423}{11600} = 36.465\,mV
$$

$$
I_D = I_0'\left[e^{\frac{V_D}{\eta V_T}} - 1\right]
$$

Assume diode is Ge, $\eta = 1$

$$
I_D = 8.192n\left[e^{\frac{0.5\times11600}{423}} - 1\right]
$$

$$
I_D = 7.383\,mA
$$

$$
r_d = \frac{\eta V_T}{I_0' + I_D} = \frac{1\times36.465m}{8.192n + 7.383m} = 4.939\,\Omega
$$

Assume diode is Si, $\eta = 2$

$$
I_D = 8.192n\left[e^{\frac{0.5\times11600}{2\times423}} - 1\right]
$$

$$
I_D = 7.168\,\mu A
$$

$$
r_d = \frac{2\times423}{(8.192n + 7.168\mu)\times11600} = 9.378\,k\Omega
$$

**NOTE:** Based on the decimal points taken, diode current and resistance can vary. Please consider the diode current and resistance values with $\pm (10 \text{ to } 15)\%$ tolerance while evaluating the answer scripts.

examples.subject: Fundamentals of Electronics
examples.markdown:
For the circuit shown in Fig. find the maximum and minimum values of zener diode current

Voltage across 5 kΩ = 120 - 50 = 70 V

Current through 5 kΩ, $I = \dfrac{70\ \text{V}}{5\ \text{k}\Omega} = 14\ \text{mA}$

Load current, $I_L = \dfrac{50\ \text{V}}{10\ \text{k}\Omega} = 5\ \text{mA}$

Applying Kirchhoff's first law, $I = I_L + I_Z$

∴ Zener current, $I_Z = I - I_L = 14 - 5 = 9\ \text{mA}$

Minimum Zener current: The zener will conduct minimum current when the input voltage is minimum i.e. 80 V. Under such conditions, we have,

Voltage across 5 kΩ = 80 - 50 = 30 V

Current through 5 kΩ, $I = \dfrac{30\ \text{V}}{5\ \text{k}\Omega} = 6\ \text{mA}$

Load current, $I_L = 5\ \text{mA}$

∴ Zener current, $I_Z = I - I_L = 6 - 5 = 1\ \text{mA}$
